import re
from typing import Tuple

def check_email(email: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """
    Check if the provided email address is valid according to RFC standards.
    
    Args:
        email: The email to check.
        
    Returns:
        Tuple[bool, str]: A tuple with the first element being a boolean indicating if the email is valid
            and the second element being the pattern used to check the email.
    """
    
    # Define an improved regular expression pattern that aligns more closely with RFC 5322 standards
    email_pattern = r"^(?:[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*|\"(?:[\x01-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x21\x23-\x5b\x5d-\x7f]|\\[\x02\x03\x09\x0c\x0d\x0a\x4a-\x4d\x6a-\x6f\x73\x74\x76\x77\x79\x7a\x7b\x7c\x7e])*\")@(?:(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?|\[(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|[01]?[0-9][0-9]?))\])$"
    
    # Use re.fullmatch to ensure the entire string matches the pattern
    is_valid = bool(re.fullmatch(email_pattern, email))
    
    return (is_valid, email_pattern)
